open_points.subject: request_password_reset
open_points.text: - request_password_reset: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST return None for both known and unknown normalized email; for a known eligible account it commits the R10 challenge and audit before delivery without exposing existence.
open_points.other_text: - request_password_reset: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST answer every presented value identically and return None on every path, including a malformed address: it normalizes the address and, when normalization rejects the value, MUST catch that rejection and still return None, because this surface is unauthenticated and answering one shape of input with an error and another with silence is itself a distinguishable answer. While the challenge records it would issue have no persistence, it MUST open no transaction, read no account, append no audit and deliver no message, because an audit for a reset that was never issued would be a false record. This inertness is declared for the deferred challenge slice rather than left as an omission.
open_points.question: Must a known eligible account cause a transaction, account read, committed challenge, audit, and delivery, or must the function remain inert and perform none of those operations?
